messages.content: You are BioGPT, an expert compiler architect. Translate the provided natural language biological protocol into valid, deterministic BioScript code for execution on a microfluidic biochip.

Source link: https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/molecular-biosciences/articles/10.3389/fmolb.2021.782905/pdf
Paper DOI: https://doi.org/10.3389/fmolb.2021.782905

Protocol details:

ASSAY TYPE: Cell-Free Glycoprotein Biosynthesis Protocol on Digital Microfluidic Chips (Flow-Based Microfluidic System for Cell-Free Glycoprotein Biosynthesis)

REAGENTS USED:
  - Plasmid DNA Stream (pJL1-sfGFP-DQNAT-6xHis acceptor protein plasmid, energy mix, salts, and metabolites)
  - S30 Cell-Free Extract Stream (E. coli BL21 Star (DE3) S30 crude extract plus T7 RNA polymerase)
  - CjLLOs Reagent (C. jejuni lipid-linked oligosaccharides bearing the GalNAc5(Glc)Bac heptasaccharide, glycan donor for the surface-tethered CjPglB oligosaccharyltransferase)
  - Wash Buffer (PBS with 10 mM imidazole, for IMAC resin washing)
  - Elution Buffer (PBS with 300 mM imidazole, for IMAC product recovery)

STEPS:
1. Protein Synthesis Module: A plasmid/energy/salts/metabolites stream and an S30 extract/T7 RNA polymerase stream are combined at the inlet of a serpentine microfluidic chip and mixed by diffusion as they travel through the channel; each chip provides a 30 min reaction residence time, and multiple chips are linked in series (up to four chips for a 2 h total residence time) to continuously synthesize sfGFP-DQNAT-6xHis.
2. Protein Glycosylation Module: The synthesized protein stream is continuously flowed over CjPglB oligosaccharyltransferase that is site-specifically biotinylated and tethered to the channel surface (via silane-PEG5000-biotin/NeutrAvidin/biotin chemistry), together with CjLLO glycan donor; the device is held at 30 C and the reaction proceeds across a series of chips at 30 min residence time per chip, achieving up to 100% glycosylation efficiency within 2 h.
3. Protein Purification Module (Loading/Flowthrough): The glycosylated protein stream is passed through a channel packed with Ni2+-charged affinity resin held in place by an array of posts at the outlet; hexahistidine-tagged glycoprotein binds the resin while unbound material exits as the flowthrough fraction.
4. Protein Purification Module (Wash): The inlet stream is switched to wash buffer (PBS + 10 mM imidazole) at 2 uL/min to remove non-specifically bound proteins and cellular debris from the resin bed; the wash fraction is collected.
5. Protein Purification Module (Elution): The inlet stream is switched to elution buffer (PBS + 300 mM imidazole) at 2 uL/min to recover the purified hexahistidine-tagged glycoprotein product as the elution fraction; the resin-bound flowthrough droplet is then discarded.

INTERPRETATION: Successful glycoprotein biosynthesis is confirmed by significantly increased sfGFP titers under continuous flow relative to batch/off-chip CFPS (Figure 2A), immunoblot detection of the monoglycosylated (g1) product with anti-His and hR6 (anti-heptasaccharide) antibodies confirming efficient on-chip glycosylation comparable to off-chip untethered reactions (Figure 3C), and recovery of purified glycoprotein product at 78 +/- 10% purity with 45 +/- 14% capture efficiency via the on-chip IMAC module (Figure 4), together demonstrating a first-in-kind modular glycosylation-on-a-chip platform for continuous, decentralized glycoprotein biomanufacturing.

identity.protocol_name: Glycosylation-on-a-Chip: A Flow-Based Microfluidic System for Cell-Free Glycoprotein Biosynthesis (Aquino et al. 2021)

source.title: Cell-Free Glycoprotein Biosynthesis Protocol on Digital Microfluidic Chips (Flow-Based Microfluidic System for Cell-Free Glycoprotein Biosynthesis)

ir.content:
main:
	plasmid1[0] = dispense(plasmid_dna)
	extract1[0] = dispense(s30_extract)
	cfps_mix1[0] = mix(plasmid1[0], extract1[0]) @ 1800.0SECOND
bsbbr_2_h:
	PHI REPEAT_31 = {REPEAT_30,REPEAT_32}
	PHI cfps_mix2 = {cfps_mix1,cfps_mix3}
	if REPEAT_31[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_3_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_4_f
bsbbr_3_t:
	cfps_mix3[0] = mix(cfps_mix2[0], cfps_mix2[0]) @ 1800.0SECOND
	REPEAT_32[0] = REPEAT_31[0] - 1
bsbbr_4_f:
	sfgfp_reading1[0] = detect(fluorescence, cfps_mix2[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	llo1[0] = dispense(cjllos_reagent)
	glyco_mix1[0] = mix(cfps_mix2[0], llo1[0]) @ 1800.0SECOND
	heat(glyco_mix1[0]) @ 30.0CELSIUS @ 1800.0SECOND
bsbbr_5_h:
	PHI glyco_mix2 = {glyco_mix1,glyco_mix3}
	PHI REPEAT_33 = {REPEAT_31,REPEAT_34}
	if REPEAT_33[0] > 0	|	true: jump bsbbr_6_t	|	false: jump bsbbr_7_f
bsbbr_6_t:
	glyco_mix3[0] = mix(glyco_mix2[0], glyco_mix2[0]) @ 1800.0SECOND
	heat(glyco_mix3[0]) @ 30.0CELSIUS @ 1800.0SECOND
	REPEAT_34[0] = REPEAT_33[0] - 1
bsbbr_7_f:
	glyco_reading1[0] = detect(fluorescence, glyco_mix2[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	flowthrough1[0] = mix(glyco_mix2[0], glyco_mix2[0]) @ 1.0SECOND
	flowthrough_reading1[0] = detect(fluorescence, flowthrough1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	wash1[0] = dispense(wash_buffer)
	wash_mix1[0] = mix(flowthrough1[0], wash1[0]) @ 120.0SECOND
	wash_reading1[0] = detect(fluorescence, wash_mix1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	dispose(wash_mix1[0])
	eluent1[0] = dispense(elution_buffer)
	product1[0] = mix(flowthrough1[0], eluent1[0]) @ 120.0SECOND
	product_reading1[0] = detect(fluorescence, product1[0]) @ 30.0SECOND
	if product_reading1[0] <= 0	|	true: jump bsbbif_8_t	|	false: jump bsbbif_9_f
bsbbif_8_t:
	dispose(product1[0])
bsbbif_9_f:
	PHI product2 = {product1,product}
	dispose(flowthrough1[0])
	NOP

numeric_mismatches.field: tethered CjPglB enzyme not modeled as a manifest
numeric_mismatches.note: CjPglB is site-specifically biotinylated and immobilized on the channel surface via silane-PEG5000-biotin/NeutrAvidin/biotin chemistry (Figure 3A); it is a persistent surface catalyst, not a per-reaction dispensed reagent, so BioScript's dispense/mix primitives cannot represent it distinctly from the flowing reaction volume.

numeric_mismatches.field: Ni2+-charged IMAC resin bed not modeled as a manifest
numeric_mismatches.note: The resin is packed against 25 um posts at the channel outlet as a fixed solid phase (Figure 4A); only the buffers flowed over it (wash_buffer, elution_buffer) are represented as dispensable manifests, and the binding/capture step itself is approximated with a self-mix rather than a true solid-phase-capture primitive.

numeric_mismatches.field: flow rate and serial chip-linking not modeled
numeric_mismatches.note: The paper's design relies on fixed flow rates (e.g., 2 uL/min for wash/elution) and physically linking multiple discrete chips in series via tubing to extend residence time; BioScript has no flow-rate or multi-device primitives, so residence time is approximated with repeated mix/heat durations on a single continuous droplet.

This is a placeholder conditional gate to fit BioScript's if/dispose pattern seen in other translated protocols; the paper does not describe a numeric discard threshold on the eluted product's fluorescence reading.

numeric_mismatches.field: quantitative titers, purity, and capture-efficiency figures (11.9, 9.4, 38.3 ug/mL sfGFP; 78 +/- 10% purity; 45 +/- 14% capture efficiency)
numeric_mismatches.note: These outcome measurements (Figures 2A, 4C) describe assay results, not protocol steps, and have no corresponding BioScript operation; they are reported in the INTERPRETATION but are not encoded as instructions.

metadata.notes: This protocol details Cell-Free Glycoprotein Biosynthesis Protocol on Digital Microfluidic Chips (Flow-Based Microfluidic System for Cell-Free Glycoprotein Biosynthesis). The assay is performed on a Digital Microfluidics (DMF) platform. Key reagents used in the assay include Plasmid DNA Stream and S30 Cell-Free Extract Stream.
